findings.title: The hit radius for starting a wire drag is capped at 8 world units (about 7dp), so misses move the component or leave dangling wires
findings.evidence: CanvasInteraction.kt: canvasPointerTolerance(type, density, scale): mouse keeps wire=terminal=min(hit,8); touch/stylus terminal = max(wire, CanvasTouchWireToleranceDp(17dp)/scale). editToolConnectionPoint accepts ports within terminalTolerance (nearest wins, with from/short-stub guard); editToolWireStart passes terminalsInsideBodies=false so a press inside or not past the port's body edge still moves the component; Edit start reach is editStart = min(terminal, hit). CircuitCanvas uses tolerances.terminal for Wire tool start/end (editWireEnd) and draws a snap ring while pressed/dragging. Behavior PKG-06/after: behavior-wire-drag-10dp-miss.txt wire from pin A port (100,100) to pin B port (300,200); behavior-edit-drag-10dp-off-output.txt wire from output (200,300), gateMovedByPortDrag false, body drag moved gate; behavior-mouse-edit-drag-off-output.txt keeps the 8-unit mouse radius; behavior-snap-ring.txt pressed true, cleared on pinch and release. findings.evidence: CircuitSemanticOverlay.kt adds one CustomAccessibilityAction per entry of componentMenu(component) and routes each through actions.componentMenu(item, id). CircuitCanvas.kt supplies the default `componentMenu = { item, id -> if VIEW_SUBCIRCUIT currentViewSubcircuit(id) else currentComponentMenu(item, id) }`, and App.kt passes onComponentMenu = handleComponentMenu. canvasAccessibleMenu builds the list from ComponentMenu.component(...), keeps enabled items, drops Delete and Show Attributes (already covered by Remove and Edit properties) and, on a read-only canvas, keeps only ReadOnlyMenuItems. after/behavior-c42-talkback-component-menu.txt: RAM offers Edit/Clear/Load/Save contents; NOT offers Rotate left/right; the subcircuit offers Rotate and 'Ver sub'; the Edit-contents action was invoked. findings.title: No auto-pan at the canvas edge while dragging: long moves and long wires need several drags
findings.evidence: CircuitCanvas.kt: autoPans is true for every non-pan one-finger drag (MOVE_SELECTION, DRAW_WIRE, SELECT_AREA, MOVE_WIRE_CORNER, PLACE, and paste preview). It is false for mouse pan, secondary button, I/O press and pinch. autoPan() calls canvasAutoPanDelta(position, width, height, density) unless a placement is off the canvas or over the zoom controls. The loop advances time-based ticks (panClock/panTickedAt, CanvasAutoPanFrameMillis, capped at CanvasAutoPanMaxSteps) using withTimeoutOrNull waits, so a still or jittering finger keeps scrolling. After each tick it calls setView(pan + delta*steps) and dragTo(machine.position), and dragTo derives every preview from startWorld through currentView().world(position). after/behavior-c43-edge-auto-pan.txt: pan.x went 24.0 -> -177.6 and the move delta was 380 against 177 on-screen units (before: pan unchanged, delta 180). In the jitter run pan went 24.0 -> -125.5 and the drop delta equals the expected value from the final view (before-r2: pan unchanged). The screenshot shows the view scrolled with the gate under the finger at the edge.
findings.gap: Not a C43 gap, but worth recording separately: in both auto-pan scenarios the reported delta (380 and 320) is applied through moveSelected, yet the gate stays at (200,100) with undoSteps 0. CircuitEditor.move with keepConnections fails preserveConnections, because the NOT would be dragged past the wired output pin, so the move is silently refused and no status message appears. The tests assert only the reported delta, not the final position.

findings.title: Paste and Duplicate: any one-finger release commits, the preview can start off-screen, and the Apply button cannot be used on touch
findings.evidence: CircuitCanvas.kt, placingPaste branch on completion: a touch Drag only calls movePastePreview through dragTo, and only `completion is Tap || mouse` calls onCanvasTap (which pastes). The paste-confirm button ('Colar aqui' / Paste here) commits the current offset through confirmPaste. EditorState.PendingPaste has anchor = pasteAnchor(bounds), the fragment bounds centre snapped to 10. pastePreview() keeps +20/+20 unless that centre is outside the visible view, in which case it centres the preview in the viewport (both Paste and Duplicate use it). after/behavior-c45-paste-drag.txt: after the drag pendingAfterDrag=true, confirms=0, no component added, and lastPreview equals the expected canvasPoint(B). buttonOverlapsWarning=false, and the button commits exactly one paste. findings.title: No double-tap to edit a label on the canvas, and Text tool label hits are exact, so a near miss creates a new Text
findings.evidence: CircuitCanvas.kt, Tap completion: in DoubleTapLabelModes (EDIT, SELECT, MOVE), with no binding, an editable document and a component with hasLabelAttribute, a second tap on the same component within doubleTapTimeoutMillis and 2x touchSlop calls currentTextToolTap(TextToolTarget.Existing(id)). In the Text tool, the canvas calls measurer.textToolTarget(..., min(tolerances.poke, CanvasTextToolReach=12)); the mouse poke tolerance is 0, so the mouse keeps exact hits. TextTool.kt textToolTarget checks the exact label, then the exact body (it never reaches a neighbour's label), then the nearest label or body within the tolerance, and only then returns Empty. TextToolDialog labels the field AnnotationText for Text annotations. after/behavior-c46-double-tap.txt: dialog=true, prefilled E2E_IN, label changed to Cin in 1 history step (before: no dialog). behavior-c46-text-tool-near-miss.txt: the mouse gets Empty while the finger gets Existing(import-1). behavior-c46-text-tool-exact-body.txt: the finger target is import-2 after round 2 (import-1, the neighbour, before r2).

findings.title: Poke targets reuse mouse geometry: flip-flop toggle (8-unit radius), shift-register stages and PortIO pins are smaller than a fingertip
findings.evidence: CircuitCanvas.kt passes tolerances.poke, the hit radius for touch and stylus and 0 for the mouse (canvasPointerTolerance, CanvasTouchHitToleranceDp=22dp), to component.sequentialPokeTarget(world, registry, tolerances.poke). The start/end equality check uses the same tolerance. pokeReach = ceil(tolerances.poke) goes to externalIoEventAt(component, point, pokeReach). SequentialPoke.kt: the flip-flop radius is max(8, min(tol, minDimension/2)). shiftPokeTarget grows each stage box by min(tol,5) sideways and tol vertically, clipped to the body, and the nearest box wins. ExternalIoInteraction.externalIoEventAt grows pins by min(tol,2), so the 6-unit pins on a 10-unit pitch tile the whole grid without overlapping, and the nearest pin wins. With tolerance 0 all three keep the exact geometry. PKG-06 after/behavior-flip-flop-touch-poke.txt: the mouse click 12 units off-centre produced no event, while the touch tap produced FlipFlopPoked (before: none). The canvas-level evidence (PKG-06 host test, flip-flop touch poke screenshot) is from an earlier run, not re-run here.
findings.gap: By design, the PortIO pin reach is capped at 2 units, so each pin is about 10x10 units (about 10-12dp at the default zoom). Any tap within the pin grid reaches a pin, but the grid itself stays small at low zoom.

findings.title: The zoom percentage counts raw pixels, so '100%' depends on screen density and maximum zoom is too low on dense screens
findings.evidence: In the final tree the zoom is shown in dp. App.kt sets `state.canvasDensity = LocalDensity.current.density` through a SideEffect. EditorState.zoomPercent = zoomPercentOf(scale, canvasDensity) = scale/density*100 (EditorZoomControls.kt), and zoomToPercent(p) = zoomTo(p/100*density). The ceilings are in dp too: EditorState.zoomTo, CircuitCanvas zoom and pinch use MaxZoomPerDp*density, and fit/resized use FitZoomPerDp*density (ViewportState.kt). The status-bar label, its a11y text (A11yZoomExact), the slider and EditorZoomDialog (App.kt:1434, `state.zoomPercent/100f` and `zoomToPercent(it*100f)`) all read zoomPercent. No raw `scale*100` remains in the editor. WorkspaceViewport still stores px, so .circ files are unchanged. Tests: commonTest EditorHeaderZoomTest.zoomPercentCountsDensityIndependentPixels, theCeilingAndFitScaleWithTheDensity (an AND gate at density 3 now fits above 4 px/unit) and theEditorZoomsInDpAndKeepsItsCeilingInDp. jvmTest EditorHeaderMenusHostTest.zoomPercentCountsDensityIndependentPixels runs at density 3: typing 100 in Set zoom gives 3 px/unit and the label '100%', and the ceiling is 36 px with the label '1200%'. findings.title: Sequential-poke and memory-address dialogs have no title or target, and use a plain text keyboard for hex

findings.title: The PLA ROM matrix editor uses glyph-only buttons ('¬I', 'I', '·', '●') with no TalkBack descriptions
findings.evidence: In ExtraIoControls.kt, PlaRomEditor gives each input cell (a TextButton) semantics with contentDescription 'Term {t}, input I{n}' (extra_io_pla_input_cell; n counts down like the headers), stateDescription negated/direct/unused and Role.Button. findings.title: Load image on RAM/ROM rejects v2.0 raw and most other headered files (format is fixed instead of auto-detected)
findings.evidence: NativeMemoryImageActions.importImage first decodes with format=null (MemoryImageCodec.decode detects the 'v2.'/'v3.' header and parses it). It retries with the requested format only when Failure.decodableAs(format) holds (MissingFormat, InvalidUtf8 or HeaderUnsupported, MemoryEditorFileActions.kt). The canvas MEMORY_LOAD path (App.kt:724) still passes HEX_WORDS_ADDRESSED, but a headered file now decodes from its own header. The memory editor's Open file (MemoryEditorTool.kt) calls importImageWithChooser: a header is detected automatically, and a headerless or unsupported header opens MemoryFormatChoiceDialog and retries through decodeImage. Tests: commonTest NativeMemoryImageActionsTest.headeredFilesDecodeInTheFormatTheirHeaderNames ('v2.0 raw', 'v3.0 hex words plain' and 'v3.0 hex bytes plain little-endian' all succeed when HEX_WORDS_ADDRESSED is requested). jvmTest ComponentMenuActionsHostTest.memoryLoadDetectsTheHeaderOfAV2RawProgram checks the ROM `contents` equals encodeCirc(expected) with no notices. jvmTest MemoryEditorHostTest.openFileDetectsHeadersAndAsksForAFormatOtherwise covers a raw file, a headerless binary through the chooser, and an unsupported header that defaults to Binary.
findings.gap: Outside the stated impact: the canvas 'Load image…' path has no format chooser for headerless files. It falls back to HEX_WORDS_ADDRESSED, so a headerless .bin still fails there, while Evolution's MemMenu would show HexFormatDialog. The editor's Open file does offer the chooser.

findings.title: Multi-bit input value dialog ignores the pin radix, cannot take signed/float/X values, and makes the user delete the old value
findings.evidence: The new core InputValueCodec (core/.../InputValueCodec.kt) formats and parses the radixes 2, 8, 16, 10signed, 10unsigned and float. It accepts 0x/0b prefixes, accepts X only for tri-state pins, and returns localized range errors. SignalInputDialog (App.kt ~2001) is rebuilt on it. It seeds from the radix attribute (componentRegistry.attributes(component).string("radix")) and the vector value. It starts with TextFieldValue selecting the whole text, requests focus through a FocusRequester, and shows supportingText with the range hint or the error and isError. The keyboard is Number or Ascii with Characters for hex and no autocorrect. ImeAction.Done and Enter apply the value. The title names the label, radix and width. EditorState.setInputValue(id, LogicVector) drives unknown values too. The Signals strip uses the same dialog (editSignalInput, App.kt:351/1438). Tests: core InputValueCodecTest covers '-3' to 0xFD and back, '-129' range error, float 1.5 = 0x3FC00000, 'x' only when tristate, and '0b101'. jvmTest SimulationControlsHostTest.signedInputAt360/At390 checks the field shows '-3', selection (0,2), focused; typing '7' and IME Done applies 7 and closes the dialog. Evidence: PKG-08 before (initialText 253, selection 0,0, IME failed) and after (-3, focused, applied). Screenshot input-dialog-360.png shows 'Value of A (Signed decimal, 8 bits)' with '-3' selected and 'From -128 to 127'.
findings.gap: The proposed optional row of bit toggles for widths up to 16 bits was not added. It was an enhancement, not part of the described impact. No UI test drives float or X through the dialog; only the codec is tested for those.

findings.title: Changing tick frequency pauses a running simulation, drops the selection and debug copy, and adds a generic 'Edit project' undo entry
findings.evidence: EditorState.setTickFrequency(hz) writes the rate through SimulationProjectOptions.applyTo and bumps revision. It does not push undo, call onSimulationInvalidated, clear the selection or clear the debug copy, and it refuses read-only documents. App.chooseTickFrequency first calls runController.configureFrequency(hz, restartRunning=true), so a RUNNING loop restarts at the new rate; it then calls setTickFrequency. The toolbar chip (TickFrequencyControl) and the Simulate menu items both route through chooseTickFrequency. Tests: commonTest EditorStateTest.aTickFrequencyChangeKeepsTheSelectionTheHistoryAndTheRunAndIsSaved, theTickFrequencySerializesAsSimulationOptionsWritesIt (same XML as the old path), undoAndRedoKeepTheNewestTickFrequency and aReadOnlyDocumentKeepsItsTickFrequency. EditorSimulationQueueTest covers the change while RUNNING (stays RUNNING at 8 Hz, canUndo false) and aTickFrequencyChangeKeepsTheSubcircuitDebugCopy. jvmTest SimulationControlsHostTest.frequencyPickerAt360/At390 also covers this. Evidence: PKG-08 before (runAfter Executar, undo [Edit project], selection []) and after (runAfter Pausar, undo [], selection [import-1], simulationFrequency 2.0).

findings.title: Tick frequency choice: toolbar cycles 1→4→16 only, menu offers 1–64 Hz, options use free text, and frequencies above 1 kHz are shown but not honored
findings.evidence: The core TickFrequencies object holds Evolution's 24 SUPPORTED_TICK_FREQUENCIES. It offers the 13 choices from 0.25 Hz to 1 kHz (MAX_SUSTAINED_HZ, the 1 ms run-loop clamp), and choicesWith(current) keeps a stored value outside the list as a '(custom)' entry. formatTickFrequency switches to kHz ('2048 kHz', '0.25 Hz'). The toolbar chip opens a menu of radio items with the current value checked, instead of cycling 1/4/16. The Simulate menu lists the same choices under a single 'Tick frequency' heading (App.kt ~1105), so the prefix is not repeated. SimulationOptionsPanel.TickFrequencyField is now a read-only ExposedDropdownMenuBox of radio items, not free text. The chip description includes the value ('Tick frequency, 4 Hz'). For an unsustained stored rate, TickFrequencyChip shows the measured rate ('4 kHz ≈812 Hz'). Tests: core TickFrequenciesTest (the 24 supported values, the 13 choices, '2048 kHz'). jvmTest SimulationControlsHostTest.frequencyPickerAt360/390 checks 0.25–1000 are offered, 2000 is not, and choosing 2 Hz stores 2.0. Evidence: behavior-frequency-measured.txt ('4 kHz. Measured: 812 ticks/s'), behavior-frequency-custom.txt ('4 kHz (custom)' selected) and behavior-simulate-menu.txt (one heading, 13 rates).
findings.gap: Rates above 1 kHz are deliberately not offered; the reason (the run loop's 1 ms clamp) is sound. Residual: isSustained(1000.0) is true, so 1 kHz never shows a measured rate. The 4 kHz host run measured only about 812 ticks/s, which suggests a 1 kHz choice may run noticeably below its label.

findings.title: Memory editor: each word needs its own dialog, old text is not selected, and errors appear behind the dialog
findings.evidence: MemoryWordDialog (CanvasMemoryWordEditor.kt) holds a draft TextFieldValue with the whole value selected, keyed on the address. It autofocuses through a FocusRequester and keeps its own error state, with isError and supportingText showing the MemoryEditResult.Failure notice. ImeAction.Next or Done and the Previous/Next word buttons are driven by MemoryWordSteps. MemoryEditorPanel (~line 433) passes steps that commit the word, move to address±1 (changing page when needed) and keep the dialog open; the keyboard is Ascii for hex and Number otherwise. Errors no longer go to the panel behind the dialog. The stored contents change only on Apply, through MemoryImageCodec. Tests: jvmTest MemoryEditorHostTest.cellDialogSelectsTheWordStepsWithNextAndKeepsErrorsInside checks the field is focused with selection (0,2); typing '12' and IME Next moves to 'Address 1' with cell 0 = 12; '1FF' then Change shows 'The value does not fit in 8 bits.' inside the dialog with the Error semantics. Also invalidWordKeepsTheDialogOpenWithTheErrorInside, wordsAreEnteredContinuouslyAcrossAPageBoundary (four words in one dialog across a page, then Apply encodes them) and nextIsDisabledAtTheLastAddress. Screenshot phone-cell-dialog-next-error.png shows the error inside the 'Address 1' dialog with the Previous word and Next word buttons.
findings.gap: The optional on-screen hex keypad was not added; the proposal marked it optional.

findings.title: Unapplied memory edits are discarded without warning when the tool sheet is swiped down, the scrim is tapped, or Close is pressed
findings.evidence: The fix keeps the edits instead of asking before closing. MemoryEditorTool.kt: memoryEditorTool() creates a tool-level MemoryEditorDrafts keyed by MemoryEditorDraftKey(documentIdentity, circuit id, instancePath, component id). The tool is remembered in rememberBuiltInEditorTools, so it outlives the sheet. MemoryEditorPanel.kt publishes MemoryEditorDraft(base, image, stagedImport, clearLineOverflow, written) through a LaunchedEffect whenever the panel is dirty. On reopen it restores the draft (stagedImport included) and shows the 'memory-unapplied-banner' with Discard and Apply. If the memory changed underneath, it shows the 'memory-conflict-banner' instead. In App.kt the tool sheet's swipe/scrim (EditorModalSheet onDismissRequest) and header Close both only set activeTool=null, so all three paths lead to the same dispose-and-keep behaviour. Only Cancel (onDismiss) and Apply clear the draft. Screenshot PKG-09/after/phone-reopen-unapplied.png shows the edited ROM reopened with the 'Unapplied changes · Discard / Apply' banner.
findings.gap: Minor, not blocking. The host tests drive the header Close in a test harness, not the real swipe or scrim. Swipe and scrim reach the same activeTool=null path in App.kt. No test covers a staged import surviving close, although stagedImport is part of the draft. Switching to another document drops drafts silently (retainDocument).

findings.title: Signal recording pauses the simulation and has no run/tick controls, so waveforms cannot be watched while simulating
findings.evidence: TraceTool.kt now builds the trace tool with pausesSimulation=false. App.kt checks `if (tool.pausesSimulation) runController.pause()` both in openTool (around line 645) and in the Simulate-menu toolsIn loop (around line 951), so opening the trace no longer pauses the run. TracePanel takes TraceSimulationControls (Run/Pause, Tick half, Tick full) wired to context.startSimulation/pauseSimulation/stepClock. traceFollowWindow keeps the newest sample in view. The host test runs the real App: it starts Run, opens Simulate > Signal recording, then checks the run stays active and ticks advance. It pauses from the panel, taps trace-sim-tick twice, and asserts ticks +2 and samples +2. The W2-03 and INT-trace behavior-trace-run-controls.txt records runningAfterOpen=true, ticksAdvancedWhileOpen=true, samplesBefore 6 and samplesAfter 8. behavior-trace-follow.txt shows the window moving from 0..20 to 11..31.
findings.gap: The optional docked panel for wide layouts was explicitly deferred, and the trace is still a modal sheet. The user cannot poke canvas inputs while watching the trace, but run and tick, the core scenario, work from inside the panel. I agree with treating the docked panel as optional.

findings.title: Navigating into a subcircuit (or switching circuit) silently pauses the running simulation
findings.evidence: The unconditional navigation pause is gone. App.kt now runs `LaunchedEffect(state.activeCircuitName, state.activeInstancePath) { pauseOutsideRunningCircuit(state, runController) }`. In SimulationNavigation.kt, pauseOutsideRunningCircuit returns early unless viewsOutsideRunningCircuit() is true, i.e. an empty instancePath on a circuit other than main. In that case it calls pauseContinuousExecution, which keeps queued releases, and reports 'Simulation paused: {circuit} is not part of the running circuit'. No other App.kt path pauses on viewSubcircuitInstance (the call near line 1267 only navigates). W2-03/after/behavior-navigation-run.txt records instancePath=sub, runningInInstance=true, instanceTicksAdvanced=true, pausedOnOtherCircuit=true and the status text.
findings.gap: Minor. The test checks that projected instance ticks advance, not that a counter value inside the instance changes.

findings.title: Test vectors must be typed by hand, are lost when the sheet closes, and the circuit is chosen from ✓-prefixed text buttons
findings.evidence: All three problems in the user impact are fixed. (1) Opening a file: testVectorEditorTool(registry, assets) receives DocumentAssetActions from createBuiltInEditorTools. The 'vector-open-file' button calls assets.open(text/plain, application/octet-stream, 1 MiB) and decodes UTF-8 with an optional BOM (decodeVectorFile). Opening asks before replacing unsaved typed text. (2) Persistence: TestVectorToolState is created once per tool in the factory and holds text, circuitName, session, notice and failure. bind() clears it only for a different document; a project change drops only the stale session. (3) Circuit choice: TestVectorPanel uses ChoiceDropdown (SelectionControls.kt), an ExposedDropdownMenuBox listing every circuit with semantics selected on the chosen item, replacing the row of '✓'-prefixed buttons. The host test opens a fake file, closes and reopens the sheet with the text kept, then checks that all 4 circuits are listed and option 0 is selected.
findings.gap: The deferred dirty-text guard's stated reason, that no App-level guard API exists in this tree, is inaccurate: EditorSheetDraft/EditorSheetDismissGuard exist in EditorSheetDraftGuard.kt. Closing the sheet no longer needs a guard because the text persists. Switching documents still clears typed vectors silently (bind on a new documentIdentity). That is outside this finding's impact and should be tracked separately.

findings.title: Diagnostics 'Go to origin' navigates behind the open sheet, so the button appears to do nothing
findings.evidence: DiagnosticPanel.kt: diagnosticNavigation(context) calls context.navigate(target.editorLocation()) and then context.closeTool(). diagnosticsEditorTool passes it as onNavigate. In App.kt, navigate=state::focusLocation (which selects the target and calls fitSelected) and closeTool={ activeTool = null }, so the sheet closes and the selected origin is framed on the canvas. The filter is held in a tool-level DiagnosticFilter, so it survives reopening.
findings.gap: The optional 'Showing <component> in <circuit>' status line and the 'Back to diagnostics' action were not added. The core problem, a sheet that stays over the canvas, is fixed.

findings.title: Simulation toolbar is icon-only with no labels or long-press tooltips, and toolbar and menu use different names for the same actions
findings.evidence: EditorChrome.kt: ChromeButton is wrapped in a Material3 TooltipBox with a PlainTooltip (tag tooltip-<id>) showing the label or description on long press or hover. The tooltip is hidden from accessibility, and there is no extra long-press action. In App.kt the bar and the Simulate menu add the same EditorToolbarAction objects (eventAction, tickAction, tickFullAction, autoTickAction, resetAction), so labels and TalkBack descriptions come from one key each. English strings: simulation_control_step_event 'Step event', simulation_control_tick_half 'Tick half cycle', simulation_control_tick_full 'Tick full cycle', simulation_control_auto_tick 'Auto-tick', a11y_reset_simulation 'Reset simulation'. A full-cycle tick (tool-tick-cycle, EditorIcon.TICK_FULL) is on the bar. The counter uses simulation_ticks 'Ticks {count}'. Reset sits after a divider in both the bar and the menu. The tooltip behavior log records shown=true, the description equal to the label and longPressActions=[].
findings.gap: Run and Pause still differ slightly: the bar says 'Run'/'Pause', the menu says 'Run simulation'/'Pause simulation'. This is cosmetic and outside the listed actions. No test asserts the bar description equals the menu label for every action, but both come from the same action object in code.

findings.title: Trace waveform does not show bus values or a time axis, and the table view's columns do not line up

findings.title: Trace navigation is button-only: no pinch or drag on the waveform, and cursor B can only be set by long press (not available to TalkBack)
findings.evidence: TracePanel.kt: the 'trace-waveforms' Box uses awaitEachGesture to handle pinch (zoom around the focal time) and horizontal-dominant drags (window.pan). Taps and vertical drags still reach the rows. An A/B segmented toggle (trace-cursor-target-a/-b) picks which cursor taps and the trace-cursor-slider move. The semantics have CustomAccessibilityActions (Zoom in/out time, Previous, Next, Set cursor B at cursor A, Set cursor A at cursor B) and a stateDescription with the window and both cursors, so TalkBack can set cursor B. findings.title: Trace signal picker lists every component in the project and shows internal IDs ('c3/c17', 'c5//0x1f') to the user
findings.evidence: core TraceSignalPicker.kt: TraceLoggable.fileNames (Pin, Clock, Probe, Tunnel, Register, Counter, flip-flops, RAM, LED, Button...) filters rows unless showAll. Selected signals are kept, and rows are grouped by instance with human paths from instanceNames ('main › ALU(120,40)', shared labels get a location). TracePanel.kt: the picker has a 'Show all components' Switch row (trace-show-all), heading-semantics group headers, and TracePickerRow shows name.label plus name.instance. TraceRow header is name.title and the Canvas contentDescription uses name.label/instance. TraceSignalOrderDialog uses nameOf() for the text and the move up/down descriptions. reference.key is now used only for LazyColumn keys, test tags and TSV/CSV export (TraceFileRecording.kt:64). behavior-trace-picker.txt has rawKeysShown [], defaultRows {a=true, g=false, alu/reg=true}, and texts 'main', 'main › inner(300,300)'. The trace-picker-default.png screenshot shows grouped rows with no internal ids.

findings.title: Memory editor navigation and selection are typed rather than tapped; the radix control and address fields are ambiguous
findings.evidence: MemoryEditorPanel.kt: MemoryRadixControl is a labelled 'Value base' SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow (Bin/Oct/Dec/Hex, contentDescription 'Binary values' and so on, selected semantics) and changes only model.valueRadix. MemoryEditorModel.addressRadix stays HEXADECIMAL. The fields are labelled memory_address_hex/memory_range_end_hex with an Ascii keyboard and autocorrect off. findings.title: Memory image format is picked from 11 bracket-marked buttons in a horizontal strip inside a non-scrolling dialog
findings.evidence: MemoryEditorPanel.kt: the 11-button strip is replaced by MemoryFormatChooser. It has four family radio rows (v2.0 raw / v3.0 hex / Binary / ASCII) built with selectable(role=RadioButton) inside selectableGroup. findings.title: Simulation warnings banner is hidden on short (landscape phone) windows, and two different warning dialogs exist

findings.title: Signals strip: unlabeled pins look identical, there is no empty state, buttons cannot be held, and multi-bit inputs are announced as 'Toggle'
findings.evidence: SignalsStrip.kt: signalStripName falls back to Messages.TraceUnnamedSignal ('Input (100,100)'). findings.title: Reset simulation wipes poked inputs and session-only RAM contents with no confirmation or undo
findings.evidence: Both the toolbar reset and the shortcut call EditorState.resetSimulation() (App.kt). The reset keeps the pre-reset simulation and drives as undoableReset. SimulationResetUndo.kt adds a 48 dp 'Undo' TextButton next to the 'Simulation reset.' status, as a polite live region. findings.title: Checkboxes without labels and selection shown only by bold or ✓/[ ] text across data panels (TalkBack)
findings.evidence: SelectionControls.kt adds LabeledCheckbox (the whole row is toggleable with role=Checkbox, and Checkbox onCheckedChange=null) and RadioOption (selectable, role=RadioButton). findings.title: Memory tool shows the raw kind name and a dead-end 'Edit' screen after Apply or Cancel, and opens empty without a selection
findings.evidence: MemoryEditorTool.kt: onApply calls context.closeTool() after showNotice on success, and onDismiss (Cancel) clears the draft and calls closeTool(). The old 'editing=false' dead-end screen showing component.kind.name has been removed. The panel title is memoryEditorTitle(component) = label or kind.localizedLabel(). An empty circuit shows 'This circuit has no ROM or RAM.'

findings.title: Trace 'Clear' deletes the whole recording instantly, with no confirmation or undo, next to 'Pause capture'
findings.evidence: In the final TracePanel.kt, the Clear TextButton (tag trace-clear) is now the last item in the toolbar row, after Export CSV and Export WaveDrom and away from Pause. When recorder.frames.size > 1 it sets confirmClear instead of clearing. The AppAlertDialog then shows trace_clear_confirm_title and the plural trace_clear_confirm_text, with Cancel and a Clear button (trace-clear-confirm) that calls clear(). Strings exist in localization/messages/tool_panels.json. The test checks the button position, that Cancel keeps all 10 frames, and that confirming leaves 1 frame. The screenshot shows the dialog text '10 captured samples will be discarded. This cannot be undone.' and Clear at the end of the toolbar. No undo snapshot was added, but the proposed fix allowed confirmation or undo.

findings.title: Dismissing the Combinational Analysis sheet (swipe, Back, scrim tap or Close) silently discards the whole truth table and every edit
findings.evidence: analysisEditorTool (AnalysisEditorTool.kt) creates one AnalysisSession per tool instance, and the tool list is kept alive by remember in rememberBuiltInEditorTools. The session (AnalyzePanel.kt, class AnalysisSession) holds the table, tableFile, page, retainedImport, forms, input/output/expression text, the selected view, the selected output, the SOP/POS form, the NAND-only setting, the table selection and undo/redo. AnalyzePanel reads this state instead of local remember. When the sheet closes, only the content leaves composition. findings.title: Trash can never be emptied, and every autosave, including pure view changes, keeps a full copy of the project forever
findings.evidence: Permanent deletion is now in place. In the final tree, WorkspaceCatalogRepository.purge(id, expectedRevision) in core/.../WorkspaceCatalog.kt works in this order: it refuses a project that is not trashed or has a stale revision, and refuses when storage.supportsDelete is false. It then commits the catalog and its backup without the project, deletes every project-<id>-* payload, and deletes attachment blobs that no other payload references.
